status: original fictional voice design; not transcriptions or impersonations
evidence_status: No new clips or audio accessed this pass. Inspiration references link to reel-analysis-2026.json sources.
global_direction: Use distinct attention and rhythm, not identical Hinglish punchlines.
Allow filler, overlap, failed jokes and silence.
Funny participants still need concrete goals unrelated to entertaining the player.
An NPC may ignore a joke; laughter never establishes consent or legal safety.
Avoid universal moral conclusions after every choice.
Use human-performed reference reads before committing voice assets; browser TTS is a preview, not performance approval.

characters.name: Kabir
characters.inner_contradiction: Wants friends to think he is unbothered; takes parental and friend approval very seriously.
characters.rhythm: Starts confidently, then repairs the sentence mid-way; talks faster when covering embarrassment.
original_example_lines: Bhai, ek second. Nahi, woh wala second nahi—phone aa raha hai.
Maine bola tha aa raha hoon. Kahan aa raha hoon, woh nahi bola.
characters.under_pressure: Lowers his voice and asks one specific friend for help.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: Uses a few borrowed English words when defending himself; never says aura to explain his own joke.

characters.name: Sharma
characters.inner_contradiction: Wants a manageable shift and respect; can be amused without abandoning a duty.
characters.rhythm: Short questions; lets the other person over-explain; occasional dry repetition of their own words.
original_example_lines: Abhi tumne bola tha dost wahin hain.
Phone pakdao. Pehle naam toh batao.
characters.under_pressure: Stops joking, gives concrete instructions; may quietly make room before publicly conceding anything.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: Not a catchphrase dispenser; irritation and kindness may coexist.

characters.name: Ravi
characters.inner_contradiction: Enjoys being indispensable; borrowed equipment and somebody else’s deposit make him anxious.
characters.rhythm: Specific nouns, interrupted counting, occasional unnecessary technical detail.
original_example_lines: Blue wire. Blue. Yeh bhi blue hai? Achha, darker blue.
Ek cup idhar mat—haan. Ab udhar hi rehne do.
characters.under_pressure: Repeats practical instructions, asks for a pair of hands rather than delivering a speech.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: His humour comes from attention landing on the wrong small detail.

characters.name: Sana
characters.inner_contradiction: Wants to help and be recognised as capable; becomes abrupt when three people ask at once.
characters.rhythm: Rapid triage questions, unfinished sentences, small sideways jokes when the immediate task is safe.
original_example_lines: Bottle khuli hai? Theek. Do glass—nahi, cup chalega.
Mujhe camera nahi, woh bag dena. Camera baad mein.
characters.under_pressure: Names a task and a person; vulnerability appears in a private pause after helping.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: Can laugh at a silly request without turning it into a lesson.

characters.name: Mira
characters.inner_contradiction: Wants a coherent public message; privately cannot keep up with every group’s needs.
characters.rhythm: Different register on microphone and beside friends; occasionally repeats a public phrase then laughs at herself.
original_example_lines: Mic pe mat bol. Mere ko bol.
Haan, sabka point hai. Ek mic hai bas.
characters.under_pressure: Makes a consequential compromise, then checks who noticed.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: No permanently wise organiser voice; she can be defensive and funny.

characters.name: Nikhil
characters.inner_contradiction: Wants to belong, is embarrassed to admit he is lost, and tracks mundane details accurately.
characters.rhythm: Literal updates arriving at inconvenient times; rarely tries to make a joke.
original_example_lines: Main wahi hoon. Wahi matlab pehle wala gate nahi.
Phone mil gaya? Achha. Charger bhi usi ke saath tha?
characters.under_pressure: Says exactly whom he cannot find, stops pretending everything is fine.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: Do not make him a perpetual helpless child. His observations can rescue a scene.

characters.name: Asha
characters.inner_contradiction: Wants ordinary work to continue and looks after familiar faces; distrusts strangers making her explain her neighbourhood.
characters.rhythm: Names people and places instead of abstractions; keeps working during a conversation.
original_example_lines: Udhar chai nahi milegi. Woh mera board ghoom gaya hai.
Pehle cup rakh. Dono haath se kahani kyun suna raha hai?
characters.under_pressure: Protects a doorway or customer, negotiates practically, remembers who actually helped.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: She is allowed to be petty, generous, bored and commercially minded.

characters.name: Farah
characters.inner_contradiction: Needs a usable story and an accurate account; worries a less careful competitor will publish first.
characters.rhythm: Precise follow-up questions; changes tone when camera is off.
original_example_lines: Usse pehle kya hua? Bas woh batao.
Yeh frame acha hai. Context abhi bhi missing hai.
characters.under_pressure: Checks one concrete discrepancy; may miss another while rushing.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: Avoid turning her into the game’s truth narrator.

characters.name: Rao
characters.inner_contradiction: Wants instructions followed and a defensible record; local improvisation can look like insubordination.
characters.rhythm: Controlled complete sentences in public; clipped phrases over radio.
original_example_lines: Mujhe dono timings chahiye. Kisne dekha?
Order clear nahi hai. Dobara confirm karo.
characters.under_pressure: Seeks confirmation, may delay, refuse or override a subordinate with consequences.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: Not automatically corrupt or automatically fair; pressure changes the available tradeoffs.

characters.name: Dev
characters.inner_contradiction: Needs different groups to believe they still have influence; sometimes promises clarity he does not possess.
characters.rhythm: Rephrases requests as agreements; cautiously corrects himself when pressed for specifics.
original_example_lines: Meeting boli hai. Time abhi nahi bola.
Haan, tumhara point andar rakha. Kis wording mein—woh bata raha hoon.
characters.under_pressure: Looks for someone to co-sign a decision; public composure and private uncertainty diverge.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: Let the player interrupt polished language with practical questions.

characters.name: Imran
characters.inner_contradiction: Has a job to finish and costs that no faction reimburses; likes a joke until it becomes his problem.
characters.rhythm: Plain practical questions with a pause before the punchline.
original_example_lines: Receipt kis ke paas hai? Payment wala nahi, delivery wala.
Sabko jaldi hai. Gaadi ko jagah bhi chahiye.
characters.under_pressure: Counts delay and damage, calls a supervisor, may help someone despite his own loss.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: No magic logistical power; no exposition about all political motives.

characters.name: Meera
characters.inner_contradiction: Wants a memorable clip; also genuinely likes the people she films and may regret her edit.
characters.rhythm: Experiments aloud with framing, then forgets the camera when something lands unexpectedly.
original_example_lines: Ek baar normal bol. Normal wala zyada funny tha.
Ruk, woh mat repeat kar. Pehli baar hi tha.
characters.under_pressure: Either puts the phone down or becomes more performative; earlier relationships determine which.
characters.anti_cringe_rule: Not every sentence contains a platform term; humour is often in what she cuts out.
